title: The dualizing map of a proper constant family
statement:
Let $S$ be the strict henselization of $\operatorname{Spec}k[t]_{(t)}$, $k$ algebraically
closed, $A$ a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of a prime $\ell$ invertible
in $k$, and let $B$ be a proper $k$-scheme with structure map $a$. For the constant family
$B\times S$ write $S_B=R\Psi_{B\times S/S}$,
$\sigma_B(L):L\to S_B(L_\eta)$ for the specialization unit and
$\theta_B:S_B\omega_{B_\eta}\to\omega_B$ for the dualizing map, the exceptional adjoint of
$Ra_!S_B\omega_{B_\eta}\xrightarrow{\nu_a}S_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Ra_{\eta!}\omega_{B_\eta}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}A$.
Then $\theta_B\circ\sigma_B(\omega_B)=\operatorname{id}_{\omega_B}$, and for every dualizing
section $z:A_{B_\eta}\to\omega_{B_\eta}$, identified with a section of $\omega_B$,

$$
 \theta_BS_B(z)\sigma_B(A)=z.
$$

proof.text:
For the constant family, $\sigma_B(\omega_B):\omega_B\to S_B\omega_{B_\eta}$ is an
isomorphism by [det-sp-constant-family-vanishing]. Proper exchange $\nu_a$ is compatible
with the specialization units (same lemma), and on the point $\operatorname{Spec}k$ the unit is the
identity, so

$$
 \nu_a\,Ra_!\sigma_B(\omega_B)
       =\sigma_{\operatorname{Spec}k}(Ra_!\omega_B)
       =\operatorname{id}_{Ra_!\omega_B}.
$$

By the definition of $\theta_B=\beta_a(A)$ as an exceptional adjoint, the map
$\theta_B\sigma_B(\omega_B):\omega_B\to\omega_B$ is the exceptional adjoint of
$\varepsilon\circ\nu_a\circ Ra_!\sigma_B(\omega_B)$, which by the display is the counit
$Ra_!\omega_B\to A$. Its exceptional adjoint is $\operatorname{id}_{\omega_B}$.

For a dualizing section $z$, naturality of $\sigma_B$ gives
$S_B(z)\sigma_B(A)=\sigma_B(\omega_B)z$, and therefore
$\theta_BS_B(z)\sigma_B(A)=\theta_B\sigma_B(\omega_B)z=z$.
